text: Lomonosov Moscow State University, often abbreviated MSU or MGU, is a coeducational and public research university located in Moscow, Russia.
Lomonosov Moscow State University was founded on January 25, 1755 by Mikhail Lomonosov, and it was renamed after Mikhail Lomonosov in 1940, when it was known as Lomonosov University.
Lomonosov Moscow State University houses the tallest educational building in the world and is rated among the universities with the best reputation in the world.
The current rector of Lomonosov Moscow State University, the research university located in Moscow, is Viktor Sadovnichiy.
Sergei Aleksandrovich Roshchin, a Russian football defender, was born on January 28, 1989 and last played for the club FC Znamya Truda Orekhovo-Zuyevo.
Sergei Aleksandrovich Roshchin's Russian name is written Сергей Александрович Рощин, and he is a defender in Russian football.
Sergei Aleksandrovich Kornilenko, born 14 June 1983, is a Belarusian professional footballer who plays as a striker for FC Krylia Sovetov Samara of the Russian Premier League.
Both Belarusian and Russian are official languages in Belarus, so Sergei Aleksandrovich Kornilenko is usually transliterated as Sergei Kornilenko and can alternatively be spelled Syarhey Karnilenka.
Sergei Aleksandrovich Chikildin, born January 25, 1991, is a Russian football goalkeeper who last played for FC Kavkaztransgaz-2005 Ryzdvyany.
Sergei Aleksandrovich Chikildin's Russian name is written Сергей Александрович Чикильдин, and his birth date is January 25, 1991.
Sergei Aleksandrovich Sholokhov is a Russian professional football player who was born on September 6, 1980.
As of August 2009, Sergei Aleksandrovich Sholokhov played in the Russian Second Division for FC Avangard Kursk.
Before 2004, Sergei Aleksandrovich Sholokhov was known as Sergei Kocherga, the Russian name Сергей Кочерга.
Sergei Aleksandrovich Panchin is a Russian football goalkeeper who was born on 15 December 1993.
Sergei Aleksandrovich Panchin's Russian name is written Сергей Александрович Панчин, and he is a goalkeeper in Russian football.
Sergei Aleksandrovich Kosarev is a Russian football midfielder who was born on January 29, 1993 and currently plays for FC MITOS Novocherkassk.
Sergei Aleksandrovich Kosarev's Russian name is written Сергей Александрович Косарев, and he is a midfielder for FC MITOS Novocherkassk.
Sergei Aleksandrovich Dmitrochenko is a Russian football midfielder who was born on June 21, 1993.
Sergei Aleksandrovich Dmitrochenko's Russian name is written Сергей Александрович Дмитроченко, and he is a midfielder in Russian football.
Sergei Aleksandrovich Tokarev was a Russian scholar and ethnographer who lived from 29 December 1899 to 19 April 1985.
Sergei Aleksandrovich Tokarev was a Russian historian, researcher of religious beliefs, and doctor of historical sciences who was a professor at Moscow State University.
Sergei Aleksandrovich Kudryavtsev (1903 to April 25, 1938) was a Ukrainian communist Soviet politician who was born in Kharkiv.
Sergei Aleksandrovich Kudryavtsev was arrested on October 13, 1937 during the Great Purge and was later executed by firing squad.
After the death of Joseph Stalin, Sergei Aleksandrovich Kudryavtsev was rehabilitated in 1956, years after his 1938 execution.

The Black Book of the Admiralty is a compilation of English admiralty law created over the course of several English monarchs' reigns, including the most important decisions of the High Court of Admiralty.
The starting point of The Black Book of the Admiralty is the Rolls of Oléron, promulgated around 1160 by Eleanor of Aquitaine, although the Black Book itself is undoubtedly later.

The Black Book of the Admiralty states that the High Court of Admiralty was established during the reign of Edward I (1272-1307), while more recent scholarship places its establishment around 1360 under Edward III.

Apart from the Rolls of Oléron, the earliest statute referred to in The Black Book of the Admiralty is the Liber memorandorum of 1338, whose separate manuscript copy is in the archives of the City of London.

The Black Book, also called The Black Book of the Holocaust, documents the ruthless murder of Jews by German-Fascist invaders in occupied Soviet regions and Nazi death camps on occupied Polish soil during 1941-1945.
The Black Book, known in Russian as Chornaya Kniga, was the result of a collaborative effort by the Jewish Anti-Fascist Committee (JAC) and members of the American Jewish community.
The Black Book also documented the participation of Jews in the fighting and resistance movement against the Nazis during World War II.
The Books of Clanranald are two paper manuscripts dating to about the early 18th century, written in Classical Gaelic and best known for their traditional account of the history of Clan Donald.
The manuscripts of the Books of Clanranald are commonly referred to as the Red Book and the Black Book, although the name Red Book may actually be a misnomer.
The name Black Book for one of the Books of Clanranald may have been coined in order to distinguish it from the so-called Red Book.
Black Book (Zwartboek) is a Dutch-language 2006 thriller novel by Laurens Abbink Spaink, and it is the novelization of the Dutch film Black Book (2006).
The novel Black Book by Laurens Abbink Spaink tells the story of a young Jewish woman, Rachel Stein, and her struggle for survival during and after the Second World War.
The novel Black Book by Laurens Abbink Spaink has a photo section and an afterword by Paul Verhoeven and Gerard Soeteman.
Black Book is an unofficial designation of optical disc (OD) formats that defy official standards for CD, DVD, HD DVD and Blu-ray Discs.
Most optical disc formats considered Black Book are used for video games or for Digital Rights Management.
Le Livre Noir du Capitalisme (The Black Book of Capitalism) is a 1998 French book published in reaction to The Black Book of Communism.

Unlike The Black Book of Communism, Le Livre Noir du Capitalisme does not primarily try to attribute a number of victims to capitalism, and its body is a series of independent works by various writers.
Le Livre Noir du Capitalisme covers topics ranging from the African slave trade to the effects of globalization.
Black Book (Zwartboek) is a 2006 Dutch thriller film co-written and directed by Paul Verhoeven and starring Carice van Houten, Sebastian Koch, Thom Hoffman, and Halina Reijn.

The 2006 film Black Book, directed by Paul Verhoeven, is about a young Jewish woman in the Netherlands who becomes a spy for the resistance during World War II after tragedy befalls her in an encounter with the Nazis.
The 2006 Dutch film Black Book had its world premiere on 1 September 2006 at the Venice Film Festival and its public release in the Netherlands on 14 September 2006.
Black Book is the first film Paul Verhoeven made in the Netherlands since The Fourth Man, which was made in 1983 before Verhoeven moved to the United States.
The Yazidi Book of Revelation, known in Kurdish as Kitêba Cilwe and also transliterated as Kitab Al Jilwah, is one of two books on the Yazidi religion written in the style of a holy book.
The Yazidi Book of Revelation is written in the Kurmanji dialect of the Northern Kurdish language, and the other book of this kind is the Yazidi Black Book, known in Kurdish as Mishefa Reş.
The original text of the Yazidi Book of Revelation is claimed to be kept in the Yazidi village of Ba'idn, while the original text of the Yazidi Black Book is kept in the village of Qasr 'tzz at-Din.
Halina Reijn is a Dutch actress and writer who was born on 10 November 1975.
Halina Reijn, a Dutch actress and writer born in 1975, is a performer and author from the Netherlands.
Neil Smith is a fiction writer who lives in Montreal, the city where he was born.
Neil Smith's most recent book, a novel called Boo, came out in May 2015 with Random House imprints in America, Britain, and Canada.
The novel Boo by Neil Smith is narrated by a young science geek named Oliver Dalrymple, who finds himself in a heaven reserved exclusively for 13-year-olds.
Neil Smith's novel Boo has been published in traditional Chinese, Czech, Dutch, French, German, and Portuguese, in addition to English.

Neil Smith's novel Boo won the Hugh MacLennan Prize for Fiction, was nominated for a Sunburst Award, an Alex Award, and the Canadian Library Association Young Adult Book Award, and received starred reviews from Publishers Weekly, Booklist, and Quill & Quire.
American Beauty is a lost 1927 American silent romantic drama film produced and distributed by First National Pictures.
The 1927 silent film American Beauty was directed by Richard Wallace and starred Billie Dove, and it was based on a short story titled American Beauty by Wallace Irwin.
In the lost 1927 film American Beauty, Billie Dove was supported by Walter McGrail and Margaret Livingston.
This is the first edition of the Miss American Beauty pageant, which was created to select a USA representative to the Miss International pageant.
A live Miss American Beauty pageant was held from 1963 to 1967, and after that time there is no actual documentation that a pageant was held to select the USA representative.
The Miss American Beauty title continued to be used for the USA representative to Miss International until approximately 2003.
Coty, Inc. is a North American beauty products manufacturer based in New York, founded in Paris, France, by François Coty in 1904.
Coty, Inc.'s main products are fragrances, colour cosmetics, and skin and body care products, and the company is known for its cooperation with designers and celebrities on fragrances.
Coty, Inc.'s power brands include Calvin Klein, Chloe, Davidoff, y, Marc Jacobs, Philosophy, Adidas, Playboy, OPI Products, Rimmel London, Max Factor, and Sally Hansen.
La Belle Américaine, English title The American Beauty, is a French comedy film from 1961, directed by Robert Dhéry and written by Alfred Adam.
The 1961 French comedy film La Belle Américaine starred Alfred Adam and Louis de Funès, with Alfred Adam also writing the screenplay.
The 1961 French comedy film La Belle Américaine was known under the titles La bella americana in Italy, The American Beauty in English, and Der tolle Amerikaner in West Germany.
American Beauty is a 1999 American drama film directed by Sam Mendes and written by Alan Ball.
Kevin Spacey stars in the 1999 film American Beauty as Lester Burnham, a middle-aged office worker who has a midlife crisis when he becomes infatuated with his teenage daughter's best friend.

American Beauty was released in North America on September 15, 1999, was positively received by critics and audiences, was the best-reviewed American film of the year, and grossed over $350 million worldwide.
At the 1999 Academy Awards, American Beauty won Best Picture, Best Director, Best Actor for Kevin Spacey, Best Original Screenplay, and Best Cinematography for Conrad Hall.
The American Beauty/American Psycho Tour was a concert tour by the American rock band Fall Out Boy, supporting its sixth studio album American Beauty/American Psycho (2015).
The American Beauty/American Psycho Tour visited North America and Europe in 2015, and its North American leg was co-headlined with the American rapper Wiz Khalifa under the name The Boys of Zummer.
The Boys of Zummer leg of the American Beauty/American Psycho Tour with Wiz Khalifa ranked fifty-ninth on Pollstar's Year End Top 200 North American Tours of 2015, grossing $18.2 million.
The Kids Aren't Alright is a song by the American rock band Fall Out Boy, released on December 15, 2014 as the first promotional single from their sixth studio album American Beauty/American Psycho.

The Kids Aren't Alright was released as a digital download with pre-orders of the album American Beauty/American Psycho, and it coincided with the release of the album's second official single, along with the album artwork and track listing.
Asked which track on American Beauty/American Psycho the band was most proud of, Pete Wentz said it was hard to say, and that Patrick says The Kids Aren't Alright.
Christopher Greenbury, ACE (September 24, 1951 to January 4, 2007) was a British film editor with more than thirty film credits dating from 1979's The Muppet Movie.
With Tariq Anwar, Christopher Greenbury won the BAFTA Award for Best Editing for American Beauty (1999), and he was also nominated for an Academy Award for Best Film Editing for that film.
Christopher Greenbury mainly edited comedy films, including six directed by the Farrelly brothers beginning with the 1994 film Dumb and Dumber.
American Beauty is a 1999 American drama film directed by Sam Mendes and written by Alan Ball, in which Kevin Spacey stars as Lester Burnham, a 42-year-old advertising executive.

In American Beauty, Annette Bening co-stars as Lester Burnham's materialistic wife Carolyn, Thora Birch plays their insecure daughter Jane, and Mena Suvari plays Angela, the teenage daughter's best friend.
Wes Bentley, Chris Cooper, and Allison Janney also appear in the 1999 film American Beauty, which academics describe as a satire of American middle-class notions of beauty and personal satisfaction.
American Beauty: Music from the Original Motion Picture Soundtrack is the soundtrack album to the 1999 film American Beauty, which starred Kevin Spacey and Annette Bening.
The soundtrack album American Beauty: Music from the Original Motion Picture Soundtrack accompanies the 1999 film in which Kevin Spacey and Annette Bening starred.
The Florida Senate is the upper house of the legislature of the U.S. state of Florida, and along with the Florida House of Representatives it composes the Florida Legislature.
The Florida Senate has 40 members, each elected from a single-member district with a population of about 470,000.
The Florida Senate, the upper house of the Florida Legislature, meets at the State Capitol in Tallahassee.
The Wisconsin Legislature is the state legislature of the U.S. state of Wisconsin, a bicameral body composed of the upper Wisconsin State Senate and the lower Wisconsin State Assembly.
Both the Wisconsin State Senate and the Wisconsin State Assembly, which together form the Wisconsin Legislature, have had Republican majorities since January 2011.
With both houses combined, the Wisconsin Legislature has 132 members representing an equal number of constituent districts, and it convenes at the state capitol in Madison.
Ken Pruitt, born January 24, 1957, was a Republican member of the Florida Senate, representing the 28th District from 2000 to 2009.
The 28th District represented by Ken Pruitt in the Florida Senate includes portions of Indian River, Martin, Okeechobee, Palm Beach, and St. Lucie Counties.
Before serving in the Florida Senate, Ken Pruitt was a member of the Florida House of Representatives from 1990 through 2000.
The Senate of Burkina Faso is an uncreated legislative upper chamber under the amended Constitution of Burkina Faso.
The original upper house of Burkina Faso, the Chamber of Representatives, was abolished in 2002, which made the country's legislature unicameral.

The June 2012 constitutional amendments of Burkina Faso were meant to restore the upper house under the name Senate, but this revision was never executed due to an extended and unresolved political confrontation.
As of the October 2014 constitutional crisis, Burkina Faso effectively had a unicameral legislature because the Senate was never established.
Murtaza A. Khan is a Member of the Legislative Council in the State of Jammu and Kashmir, India, and was elected to the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Council in February 2007.
Murtaza A. Khan was born in village Narol of Poonch District in the Indian Administered State of Jammu and Kashmir and is a well known lawyer and widely travelled person.
Murtaza A. Khan earned a bachelor's degree in law from Aligarh Muslim University and a master's degree from the USA, and he practised law in Canada before returning to Jammu and Kashmir.
Murtaza A. Khan was a founder member of the Jammu and Kashmir Peoples Democratic Party in July 1999, authored its Constitution, and was appointed PDP's General Secretary in August 2007.
Murtaza A. Khan is leader of the PDP's legislature party in the Upper House and commands the support of the Punjabi and Pothwari/Pahari speaking Muslim communities across Jammu and Kashmir.
The New South Wales Legislative Council, or upper house, is one of the two chambers of the parliament of the Australian state of New South Wales, the other being the Legislative Assembly.
Both the New South Wales Legislative Council and the Legislative Assembly sit at Parliament House in the state capital, Sydney.
The New South Wales Legislative Council has 42 members, elected by proportional representation in which the whole state is treated as a single electorate.

Members of the New South Wales Legislative Council serve eight-year terms, staggered so that half the Council is up for election every four years, roughly coinciding with Legislative Assembly elections.
Legislation in New South Wales is normally first deliberated on and enacted in the Legislative Assembly, then considered in the Legislative Council, which acts in the main as a house of review.

The Nevada Legislature is the state legislature of the U.S. state of Nevada and is a bicameral body consisting of the lower Nevada Assembly, with 42 members, and the upper Nevada Senate, with 21 members.
All 63 members of the Nevada Legislature are elected from an equal number of constituent districts across the state.
The Nevada Legislature is the third smallest bicameral state legislature in the United States, after the Alaska Legislature with 60 members and the Delaware General Assembly with 62 members.
An upper house, sometimes called a Senate, is one of two chambers of a bicameral legislature, or one of three chambers of a tricameral legislature, the other chamber being the lower house.
The house formally designated as the upper house is usually smaller than the lower house and often has more restricted power.
Examples of upper houses include the UK's House of Lords, India's Rajya Sabha, Russia's Federation Council, Ireland's Seanad, Germany's Bundesrat, and the United States Senate.

The Alaska Legislature is the state legislature of the U.S. state of Alaska, a bicameral institution consisting of the lower Alaska House of Representatives, with 40 members, and the upper Alaska Senate, with 20 members.
The Alaska Legislature has 40 House Districts numbered 1 to 40 and 20 Senate Districts lettered A to T.

With a total of 60 lawmakers, the Alaska Legislature is the smallest bicameral state legislature in the United States and the second-smallest of all state legislatures, after the 49-member unicameral Nebraska Legislature.
There are no term limits for either the Alaska House of Representatives or the Alaska Senate.
Elections to the Upper House of the Althing, the legislature of Iceland, were held in Iceland on 15 June 1930.

Following reforms in 1915, the six seats in the Upper House of the Althing that were appointed by the monarch were abolished and replaced with six seats elected by proportional representation at the national level using the D'Hondt method.
The remaining eight seats of the Upper House of the Althing were elected along with the Lower House in the 1930 election, which was the last election solely for the Upper House.
From 1934 onwards, all members of the Upper House of the Althing were elected together with the Lower House.
The list of notable species of the agaric genus Amanita is far from exhaustive, since the genus contains over 500 named species and varieties.

The list of notable Amanita species follows the classification of subgenera and sections of Amanita outlined by Corner and Bas, as used by Tulloss (2007), modified by Redhead et al. (2016) for subgenus Amanitina, and by Singer for section Roanokenses.
In the list of notable Amanita species, a bolded species name followed by an asterisk indicates the type species of that section, and a double asterisk indicates the type species of the entire genus.
Common names in the list of notable Amanita species follow Tulloss (2007), Holden (2003), Arora (1986), and Lincoff (1981).
The Calyptocephalellidae are a family of toads found in Chile, containing two genera, Calyptocephalella and Telmatobufo.
The genus Calyptocephalella contains one species, C. gayi, the helmeted water toad, which is a large aquatic toad weighing up to 0.5 kg.
The genus Telmatobufo, part of the Calyptocephalellidae toad family, contains four species: T. australis, T. bullocki, T. ignotus, and T. venustus.
All species within the Calyptocephalellidae family are considered threatened, with Telmatobufo bullocki and Telmatobufo venustus classified as critically endangered.
Leptofoenus is a genus of wasp in the family Pteromalidae, the type genus of the subfamily Leptofoeninae, found in South, Central, and southern North America.
The Leptofoenus genus contains five living species and one extinct species known from early Miocene Burdigalian stage Dominican amber deposits on the island of Hispaniola.
Leptofoenus wasps are larger than nearly all other species in the family Pteromalidae, and the genus bears a notable resemblance to the wasp families Pelecinidae, Gasteruptiidae, and Stephanidae.
Banksiamyces is a genus of fungi in the order Helotiales, with a tentative placement in the family Helotiaceae, and it contains four species.
The Banksiamyces fungi grow on the seed follicles of dead infructescences, or cones, of various Banksia species, a genus in the plant family Proteaceae endemic to Australia.
Banksiamyces fruit bodies appear as small, typically less than 10 mm diameter, shallow dark cups on Banksia follicles, and their dry edges fold inwards, appearing like narrow slits.

The first Banksiamyces specimens, then known as Tympanis toomansis, were described in 1887, and in the early 1980s a new genus was created to contain three species: B. katerinae, B. macrocarpus, and B. toomansis.
The fourth Banksiamyces species, B. maccannii, was added to the Banksiamyces genus of fungi in 1984, after the three original species were established.
Megalurus is a genus of passerine birds in the family Locustellidae, and the genus was once placed in the Old World warbler wastebin family Sylviidae.
The Megalurus genus contains six species, known as the typical grassbirds, distributed from northern China and Japan to India in the west and Australia in the south.

The most widespread Megalurus species, the tawny grassbird, ranges from the Philippines to southern New South Wales, while the Fly River grassbird is restricted to swampland in the southern part of New Guinea.
The typical grassbirds of the Megalurus genus live in wet grasslands, swamps, and other marshlands, and some species have adapted to the margins of rice fields and gardens.
Greyia is a genus of plant in the family Melianthaceae, and the genus contains three species.
The plant family Melianthaceae includes the genus Greyia, which the source describes as containing three species.
Lophodermium is a genus of fungi within the family Rhytismataceae, containing 145 species with a global distribution.
Lophodermium species are usually observed producing zone lines, conidiomata, and ascomata on dead fallen leaves, but at least some are known to colonize living leaves.

Many Lophodermium species live inside the colonized leaf as symptomless endobionts, where they are regarded as detritivores utilising dead plant matter, while a few kill all or part of the leaf prematurely.

The Lophodermium genus infects many plant families with a notable concentration in Pinaceae, and the species L. pinastri and L. seditiosum cause needlecast disease in European Black Pine, Scots Pine, and Red Pine.
Pachyornis is an extinct genus of ratites from New Zealand that belonged to the moa family, in the order Struthioniformes, and it contains three species.
Pachyornis moa were the stoutest and most heavy-legged genus of the moa family, and its most notable species, Pachyornis elephantopus, is known as the Heavy-Footed Moa.
Pachyornis moa differed from the Eastern Moa and the Broad-billed moa of the genus Euryapteryx by having a pointed bill and being more heavyset in general.

The Pachyornis species became rapidly extinct following human colonization of New Zealand, with the possible exception of P. australis, which may already have been extinct by then and is assumed to have had a crest of long feathers.
Calibanus is a genus of two species of flowering plants, both evergreen succulents from dry areas of northeastern Mexico.
The APG III classification system places the Calibanus genus in the family Asparagaceae, subfamily Nolinoideae, having separated it from the Agavaceae because Calibanus is polycarpic and dioecious.
The name of the plant genus Calibanus refers to the monster Caliban, an antagonist in Shakespeare's The Tempest.
Ceratozamia is a genus of New World cycads in the family Zamiaceae, containing 27 known currently living species and one or two fossil species.
Most Ceratozamia species are endemic to mountainous areas of Mexico, while a few species extend into the mountains of Guatemala, Honduras, and Belize.
The genus name Ceratozamia comes from the Greek word ceras, meaning horn, which refers to the paired, spreading horny projections on the male and female sporophylls of all species.
Tom Clancy's Net Force Explorers, also called Net Force Explorers, is a series of young adult novels created by Tom Clancy and Steve Pieczenik.
Tom Clancy's Net Force Explorers is a spin-off of the military fiction series Tom Clancy's Net Force.
Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon 2: Summit Strike is the expansion to the game Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon 2, and there are several minor differences between the two games.
The most notable difference between Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon 2: Summit Strike and Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon 2 is the difficulty, as Summit Strike is regarded as the harder of the two.
Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon 2: Summit Strike adds new multiplayer modes, such as Heli Hunt, as another difference from Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon 2.
John Hoyer Updike (March 18, 1932 to January 27, 2009) was an American novelist, poet, short story writer, art critic, and literary critic.
John Updike was one of only three writers to win the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction more than once, the others being Booth Tarkington and William Faulkner.
During his career, John Updike published more than twenty novels, more than a dozen short-story collections, and poetry, art and literary criticism, and children's books.

Thomas Leo Tom Clancy Jr. (April 12, 1947 to October 1, 2013) was an American novelist best known for his technically detailed espionage and military-science storylines set during and after the Cold War.
Seventeen of Tom Clancy's novels were bestsellers, and more than 100 million copies of Tom Clancy's books are in print.
Tom Clancy's name was also used on movie scripts written by ghost writers, nonfiction books on military subjects, and video games.
Tom Clancy was a part-owner of the Baltimore Orioles and served as vice-chairman of the team's community activities and public affairs committees.
Tom Clancy's Net Force Explorers, also called Net Force Explorers, is a series of young adult novels created by Tom Clancy and Steve Pieczenik.
Tom Clancy's Net Force Explorers is a spin-off of the military fiction series Tom Clancy's Net Force.

Tom Clancy's Net Force Explorers is a spin-off of the military fiction series Tom Clancy's Net Force.
Tom Clancy's Rainbow 6: Patriots is a cancelled first-person shooter video game in the Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six series, announced on the cover of the December 2011 issue of Game Informer.
Tom Clancy's Rainbow 6: Patriots was to be published by Ubisoft and developed by Ubisoft's Montreal studio, with additional development by Ubisoft Toronto and Red Storm Entertainment.
After the death of Tom Clancy in October 2013, Ubisoft stated that it will continue putting Tom Clancy's name on future Tom Clancy titles out of respect for the late author.

Tom Clancy's Net Force Explorers is a spin-off of the military fiction series Tom Clancy's Net Force.

Benjamin Lincoln (January 24, 1733 to May 9, 1810) was an American army officer who served as a major general in the Continental Army during the American Revolutionary War.

Benjamin Lincoln was involved in three major surrenders during the war, and his participation in the Battles of Saratoga, where he sustained a wound shortly afterward, contributed to John Burgoyne's surrender of a British army.
Benjamin Lincoln oversaw the largest American surrender of the war at the 1780 Siege of Charleston.
As George Washington's second in command, Benjamin Lincoln formally accepted the British surrender at Yorktown.

The 1st Virginia State Regiment was a regiment of Virginia Militia that fought during the American Revolutionary War, authorized by the General Assembly of Virginia in December 1776 as a force of regular troops.
In July 1777, under the command of Colonel George Gibson, the 1st Virginia State Regiment began a march north to temporarily join the Continental Army in the Philadelphia Campaign.

In January 1778, the Virginia General Assembly directed that the 1st Virginia State Regiment be continued in Continental service instead of the Ninth Virginia Regiment, which had been made prisoner by the enemy in the Battle of Germantown.

The 1st Virginia State Regiment camped at Valley Forge in the winter of 1777-78 and at Middlebrook in the winter of 1778-79, participated in the Battle of Monmouth, and remained in Continental Army service until late 1779, when it was redeployed to Virginia.
Unlike the standard division of eight companies found in regular line regiments of the Continental Army, the 1st Virginia State Regiment consisted of ten companies, including one of light infantry.

The Siege of Yorktown, ending on October 19, 1781 at Yorktown, Virginia, was a decisive victory by a combined force of Continental Army troops led by General George Washington and French Army troops led by the Comte de Rochambeau.

The Siege of Yorktown defeated a British Army commanded by British peer and Lieutenant General Charles Cornwallis, and the surrender of Cornwallis and his army prompted the British government to negotiate an end to the conflict.

The Siege of Yorktown was the last major land battle of the American Revolutionary War in the North American theater, and it boosted faltering American morale and revived French enthusiasm for the war.
Benedict Arnold (January 14, 1741 to June 14, 1801) was a general during the American Revolutionary War who fought for the Continental Army and later defected to the British Army.

While a general on the American side, Benedict Arnold obtained command of the fortifications at West Point, New York, and planned to surrender them to British forces, a plan that was exposed in September 1780.
After defecting to the British side, Benedict Arnold was commissioned into the British Army as a brigadier general.
The Battle of Germantown was a major engagement in the Philadelphia campaign of the American Revolutionary War, fought on October 4, 1777 at Germantown, Pennsylvania.
At the Battle of Germantown, the British Army led by Sir William Howe fought the American Continental Army, which included the 2nd Canadian Regiment, under George Washington.

The Board of War, also known as the Board of War and Ordnance, was created by the Second Continental Congress as a special standing committee to oversee the American Continental Army's administration and make recommendations to Congress.

Pressure from George Washington and the large volume of military business led the Second Continental Congress to establish the Board of War and Ordnance on June 12, 1776, after Edward Rutledge had suggested a war office similar to Britain's on January 24, 1776.
The five initial delegates of the Board of War were John Adams, Roger Sherman, Benjamin Harrison, James Wilson, and Edward Rutledge, assisted by a permanent secretary, Richard Peters.
The Board of War began functioning on June 21, 1776, with responsibilities that included compiling a master roster of all Continental Army officers and securing prisoners of war.
John André (2 May 1750 to 2 October 1780) was a British Army officer who was hanged as a spy by the Continental Army during the American Revolutionary War.
John André was hanged as a spy for assisting Benedict Arnold's attempted surrender of the fort at West Point, New York, to the British.

The United States National Memorial Arch, located in Valley Forge National Historical Park in Chester County, Pennsylvania, is a monument built to celebrate the arrival of General George Washington and the Continental Army at Valley Forge.
Valley Forge was the military camp 18 miles northwest of Philadelphia where the American Continental Army spent the winter of 1777-78 during the American Revolutionary War.
Starvation, disease, malnutrition, and exposure killed more than 2,500 American soldiers at Valley Forge by the end of February 1778.

The Continental Army was the national army of first the Thirteen Colonies and then the independent United States during the American Revolutionary War, established by a resolution of the Continental Congress on June 14, 1775, three days before the Battle of Bunker Hill.

In the spring of 1775 the Continental Congress took a number of steps to create the Continental Army in response to the Battles of Lexington and Concord in April and the seizure of Fort Ticonderoga in May.

The units composing the Continental Army changed frequently, especially in its first two years of the war, and from 1777 to the close of the war its organization became progressively more systematic and sophisticated.
The Continental Army that served at Yorktown in 1781 bore very little resemblance to the Continental Army that blockaded Boston in 1775.
Pulaski's Legion was raised on March 28, 1778 at Baltimore, Maryland, under the command of Kazimierz Pulaski for service with the Continental Army during the American Revolutionary War.
Pulaski's Legion consisted of one troop of lancers, two troops of dragoons, and 200 light infantry soldiers.
Pulaski's Legion, raised by Kazimierz Pulaski, was one of the few cavalry regiments in the American Continental Army.

Béatrice Picard, born July 3, 1929 in Montreal, Quebec, is a Canadian actress who is well known in Quebec for roles on the French Canadian theatre and television scene over an acting career spanning more than six decades.

Béatrice Picard became a household name in Quebec for her role as Angelina Desmarais in Le survenant, one of the first French Canadian télé-roman series in the early days of French-speaking television.
Béatrice Picard went on to appear in televised comedies such as Cré Basil and Symphorien, and she is the Quebec French voice of Marge Simpson in The Simpsons.
Emmanuel Curtil, born 7 February 1971, is a French actor known primarily for his voice work.
Emmanuel Curtil dubbed the voice of Matthew Perry as Chandler for the first eight seasons of the American sitcom Friends.
Emmanuel Curtil is the French voice of Jim Carrey and the current voice of Goofy, having taken over the role from Gérard Rinaldi, who died in 2012.
Ethel Houbiers is a French voice actress who is the French voice of Penélope Cruz and Salma Hayek.
The French voice actress Ethel Houbiers provides the French dubbing voice for the actresses Penélope Cruz and Salma Hayek.
Salma Hayek Pinault, born Salma Hayek Jiménez on September 2, 1966, is known professionally as Salma Hayek and is a Mexican and American film actress, producer, and former model.
Salma Hayek began her career in Mexico starring in the telenovela Teresa and in the film El Callejón de los Milagros (Miracle Alley), for which she was nominated for an Ariel Award.
In 1991 Salma Hayek moved to Hollywood and came to prominence with roles in movies such as Desperado (1995), From Dusk Till Dawn (1996), Dogma (1999), and Wild Wild West (1999).
Dorothée Jemma, a French voice actress specializing in dubbing, was born on June 16, 1956.
Dorothée Jemma is the French dub voice of the actresses Jennifer Aniston, Melanie Griffith, and Sheryl Lee.
Roger Carel, born Roger Bancharel on 14 August 1927, is a French actor and voice talent who was born in Paris, France.
Roger Carel is known for his recurring film roles as Asterix, and as the French voice of C-3PO in Star Wars and of Winnie the Pooh.
Roger Carel is dubbing David Suchet as Hercule Poirot in Agatha Christie's Poirot, and he voiced Wally Gator, Mickey Mouse, and Woody Woodpecker in French.
Lisette Dufour, born in 1949, is a Québécoise voice actress who is better known as the French voice of Lisa Simpson on The Simpsons.
Lisette Dufour is a Québécoise voice actress best known for providing the French voice of Lisa Simpson.
Bernard Alane, born Bernard Noël Vetel on 25 December 1948 in Paris, is a French actor and singer who is the son of actress Annick Alane.
Bernard Alane is best known in France for his roles in the films Hibernatus and Mon oncle Benjamin, both directed by Edouard Molinaro.
Bernard Alane is the official French voice of Stanley Tucci and Ray Liotta, and he has achieved greater fame as a voice actor, practically in dubbing.
Virginie Ledieu, a French voice actress who specializes in dubbing, was born on August 2, 1960.
Virginie Ledieu is the daughter of Marion Game and the official dubbing voice of Alyson Hannigan.
Mary Forbes (30 December 1883 to 22 July 1974) was a British film actress who was based in the United States in her latter years, and she died there.
Mary Forbes, the British film actress, appeared in more than 130 films between 1919 and 1958.

Mary Forbes's legal name was Mrs. Ethel Louise Taylor, later Quartermaine and later still Wall, according to her son's 6 November 1904 baptismal record, though it is unclear whether Forbes was her maiden name.
The dates and lengths of the three marriages of the British actress Mary Forbes are unknown.
Dubai International Airport (IATA: DXB, ICAO: OMDB) is the primary international airport serving Dubai, United Arab Emirates, and it is the world's busiest airport by international passenger traffic.
Dubai International Airport is the 3rd busiest airport in the world by passenger traffic and the 6th busiest cargo airport in the world.
Dubai International Airport is the busiest airport for Airbus A380 and Boeing 777 movements and the busiest airport in the world operating with only two runways.
In 2016, Dubai International Airport handled 83.6 million passengers, 2.59 million tonnes of cargo, and 418,220 aircraft movements.
Gatwick Airport, also known as London Gatwick (IATA: LGW, ICAO: EGKK), is a major international airport in south-east England, 29.5 mi south of Central London and 2.7 NM north of Crawley.
Gatwick Airport is the second-busiest airport by total passenger traffic in the United Kingdom, after London Heathrow, and the eighth-busiest airport in Europe.
Until 2016, London Gatwick was the busiest single-use runway airport in the world, before being overtaken by Mumbai's Chhatrapati Shivaji International Airport.
Coimbatore International Airport (IATA: CJB, ICAO: VOCB) is the primary airport serving the city of Coimbatore in Tamil Nadu, located at Peelamedu about 13 km from the city centre.

Previously known as Peelamedu Civil Aerodrome, Coimbatore International Airport is the 19th busiest airport in India by passengers handled, the 16th busiest by total aircraft movement, and the 14th busiest by cargo handled.

Coimbatore International Airport is the second largest airport in Tamil Nadu in terms of passenger traffic and cargo, after Chennai International Airport, and about five domestic and three international airlines serve it.
Vancouver International Airport (IATA: YVR, ICAO: CYVR) is located on Sea Island in Richmond, British Columbia, Canada, about 12 km from Downtown Vancouver.
Vancouver International Airport is the second busiest airport in Canada by aircraft movements (306,799) and by passengers (22.3 million), behind Toronto Pearson International Airport.
Vancouver International Airport won the Skytrax Best North American Airport award in 2007 and in each year from 2010 through 2017, and it is a hub for Air Canada and WestJet.
Vancouver International Airport is one of eight Canadian airports with US Border Preclearance facilities and one of the few major international airports to have a terminal for scheduled floatplanes.

Grantley Adams International Airport (GAIA, IATA: BGI, ICAO: TBPB) is the international airport of Barbados, located in Seawell, Christ Church, and it is the only designated port of entry for air arrivals and departures in Barbados.
Grantley Adams International Airport has direct service to destinations in the United States, Canada, Central America, and Europe, and it serves as the second hub for LIAT.

In 2016, Grantley Adams International Airport was the 8th busiest airport in the Caribbean region and the third busiest in the Lesser Antilles, after Queen Beatrix International Airport in Aruba and Pointe-à-Pitre International Airport in Guadeloupe.
Grantley Adams International Airport is a base of operations for the Regional Security System (RSS) and the Regional (Caribbean) Police Training Centre.

Croydon Airport (ICAO: EGCR) was an airport in South London, England, and it was the main airport for London before it was replaced by Northolt Aerodrome, London Heathrow Airport, and Gatwick Airport.
The terminal building and entrance lodge of the former Croydon Airport in South London are Grade II listed buildings.
Chennai International Airport (IATA: MAA, ICAO: VOMM) is an international airport serving the city of Chennai (Madras), Tamil Nadu, India, and its metropolitan area.
Chennai International Airport is the fourth busiest airport in India by total passenger traffic, after the airports at Delhi, Mumbai, and Bengaluru, and the third busiest in India for cargo handling.
In fiscal year 2016-17, Chennai International Airport handled over 18.3 million passengers, and it handles over 400 aircraft movements per day, with 49th place among Asian airports for CY 2016.
The planned extension of the terminals at Chennai International Airport was about to start, as the union government had told that Chennai might not get its new airport soon.

Dublin Airport (Irish: Aerfort Bhaile Átha Cliath; IATA: DUB, ICAO: EIDW) is an international airport serving Dublin, the capital city of Ireland, and it is operated by DAA, formerly the Dublin Airport Authority.
Dublin Airport is located 5.4 nmi north of Dublin in Collinstown, Fingal, and in 2016 it handled 27.9 million passengers, its busiest year on record.
Dublin Airport is the 15th busiest airport in Europe and the busiest of Ireland's airports by total passenger traffic, with the greatest traffic levels on the island of Ireland.

Athens International Airport Eleftherios Venizelos (IATA: ATH, ICAO: LGAV), commonly abbreviated AIA, began operation on 28 March 2001 and is the primary international airport serving the city of Athens and the region of Attica.
Athens International Airport is Greece's busiest airport and serves as the hub and main base of Aegean Airlines, as well as other Greek airlines.
As of 2016, Athens International Airport was the 27th busiest airport in Europe and was in Group 2 of Airports Council International, which covers airports handling 10 to 25 million passengers.
Heathrow Airport, also known as London Heathrow (IATA: LHR, ICAO: EGLL), is a major international airport in London, United Kingdom.
Heathrow Airport is the second busiest airport in the world by international passenger traffic, surpassed by Dubai International in 2014, and the busiest airport in Europe by passenger traffic.
In 2016, Heathrow Airport handled a record 75.7 million passengers, a 1.0% increase from 2015, and it was the seventh busiest airport in the world by total passenger traffic.
